title: Outlook for Mac and iPad: pop out Copilot Chat into a floating window
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly presents Integrated Apps as the only documented way to block Copilot in Outlook and treats enterprise data protection as unconfirmed for the floating chat. Microsoft documents broader privacy controls and enterprise protections for Copilot Chat; its pages also disagree about whether the Integrated Apps block affects Teams and can be scoped.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center path is Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. ... Select Block app.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no automation equivalent for this Integrated Apps Copilot app block.
claims.quote: Searched: Integrated Apps block Copilot Microsoft Graph PowerShell; Integrated Apps PowerShell block Outlook. Opened Integrated Apps and Manage Copilot Chat; read Update-M365TeamsApp and copilotPackage:block results, neither identifying an equivalent for this Copilot app control.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; summary; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant UI or API switch targeting the Mac and iPad pop-out alone in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Copilot Chat pop-out Mac iPad disable policy; Copilot Chat Outlook Mac iPad pop-out disable admin policy. Opened Manage Copilot Chat, Integrated Apps and Copilot release notes; no pop-out switch found.

claims.claim: The documented Integrated Apps controls require the Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app through Integrated Apps blocks Copilot Chat in Outlook and the Copilot app, rather than just its pop-out.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps block also blocks Copilot Chat in Teams.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.fix: Add: 'Manage Copilot Chat says this block includes Teams, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365 says the app is blocked only in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook, with Teams continuing to honour its Teams admin center settings.'

claims.claim: The tenant-wide Integrated Apps block can be scoped to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users.
claims.fix: Replace 'scopable to users or groups' with 'Manage Copilot Chat describes user/group scoping, but the linked Integrated Apps instructions say Block app blocks all users; those instructions document user/group selection separately under Edit Users or the Users tab.' Cite both https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/manage-copilot-chat and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps Copilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.
